❓
Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Can the best person at a skill still fall short of a goal? Look at who reaches the end of this quest, and who does not.

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
📖Reading: I will read Book Three, Chapter 6, “How Launcelot and Gawain came to Carbonek,” and Chapter 7, “The End of the Quest.”
🪞Foil: I will tell what a foil is, and which knight is Launcelot’s clearest one.
🔤Words: I will learn five words: hermit, procession, declined, accomplished, and desolate.
🪟Evidence: I will set the moments of the quest into four chapel windows.
📝Writing: I will plan Quick Write 4: one knight, one claim, two moments.

In Tennyson’s poem, Galahad rides alone toward the Grail, and in the sky he hears a sound. Here are the last twelve lines.

Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1809–1892)
0:40
AI voice reading, not a recording of Tennyson. Photograph: Julia Margaret Cameron, 1865, public domain.
🖍️ Highlighter: the voices speak to Galahad. Tap the two lines they say.
Sir Galahad
Alfred, Lord Tennyson (1842) · the last stanza
[Omitted: the first eight stanzas]
The clouds are broken in the sky, And thro’ the mountain-walls A rolling organ-harmony Swells up, and shakes and falls. Then move the trees, the copses nod, Wings flutter, voices hover clear: “O just and faithful knight of God! Ride on! the prize is near”. So pass I hostel, hall, and grange; By bridge and ford, by park and pale, All-arm’d I ride, whate’er betide, Until I find the holy Grail.
organ-harmony: music like a church organ’s · copses: small woods · hostel: an inn · grange: a farm · ford: a shallow place to cross a river · park and pale: fenced land · All-arm'd: in full armour · whate'er betide: whatever happens

🔤 Words: The End of the Quest
The other five of this week’s ten words. Tap a card to hear it.
hermit
A holy man who lives alone and gives his life to prayer.
“…Naciens, the divine Hermit of Carbonek, stood at King Pelles’ side…” Green, The End of the Quest
procession
A line of people moving slowly and formally.
“…in a beam of clear light the procession of the Grail came in for the last time.” Green, The End of the Quest
declined
Politely refused.
“But each of them declined the rich fare and the strong wine offered to them, eating only bread and drinking clear water.” Green, The End of the Quest
accomplished
Completed; brought to its end.
“Your wanderings are ended, for in this castle is the Holy Grail, and this night all things shall be accomplished.” Green, The End of the Quest
desolate
Empty, ruined and lifeless.
“…the wide lands which surround the castle and which were never more waste or desolate.” Green, The End of the Quest

Part 1Chapter ThinkingComplete sentences, with details from the text.
1. At Carbonek, Gawain rises and asks the Grail Maiden what these things mean. What happens because he asked, and what does it show about him?
2. What happens to Carbonek and the lands around it once the quest is accomplished?
3. Long after, Percivale’s kingdom “made still a little light in the darkness.” What could that light stand for?

Knight: Sir Bors.

Claim: A good knight serves the quest even when the glory goes to someone else.

Moment 1 (Ch. 1): When Galahad sits in the Siege Perilous, Bors cries that he “shall achieve great things.”

Moment 2 (Ch. 7): Bors sees everything at Carbonek, then rides home and tells the whole tale.
